# My farming plan for this year

Alright, let me think this through. I've got 225 mu — that's a lot of land for a family of four, so I depend on hired help, especially at chili picking time. I own a tractor and a sprayer, and I contract out for combining. I've been doing this 15 years so I have a pretty good sense of what the ground will do for me.

Last year my wheat came in around 480 kg/mu and the maize after it was about 520 kg/mu. Nothing fancy, but steady. The chili price was okay and the stevia buyer pays on contract, so I'm keeping both.

**Field allocation:**
- 150 mu wheat-maize double crop (my bread-and-butter rotation)
- 40 mu chili (high value but eats labor)
- 35 mu stevia (contracted, reliable cash)

**Wheat (150 mu):** I plant in early-to-mid October right after the maize comes off. Improved variety from the co-op, semi-dwarf so it doesn't fall over. Before drilling I broadcast about 30 kg DAP plus 15 kg urea per mu for the base — that's roughly 7 kg N in the DAP plus 7 in the urea, call it 14 kg N per mu at the start. At green-up in March I topdress 10 kg urea (another 5 kg N), and if the fields look weak at jointing I add 7-8 kg more. I water four times — pre-winter, green-up, jointing, grain fill. Extension tells us 15 kg N per mu is the target but I usually do a bit more because I'm chasing 500 kg yield.

**Maize (150 mu):** Straight after wheat, can't lose a day. No-till planter right into the stubble, hybrid seed. Base fertilizer goes down with the planter, about 40 kg compound (15-15-15). Topdress urea 20 kg per mu at big trumpet stage. That comes out around 16-18 kg N/mu total. I irrigate once or twice if it's dry at tasseling, usually the summer rain does most of the work. Target 550 kg/mu.

**Chili (40 mu):** This is where the money and the work both are. Transplant seedlings early May after frost risk passes. Seedlings alone run 250 yuan/mu. Heavy base fertilizer — 50 kg compound plus manure — then topdress urea 15 kg/mu after fruit set. I water 5-6 times with the well, can't let it dry at flowering. Pesticide for aphids and anthracnose, no skipping. Picking is all hired labor, runs July through September, several pickings. Expecting around 300 kg/mu dry red chili.

**Stevia (35 mu):** Planted April. This patch is in year 2 of its stand. Compound fertilizer 30 kg/mu base plus one topdress. Irrigate 3 times. Cut twice during the season, dried at home, delivered to the company on contract. Target 350 kg/mu dry leaves.

Main tradeoff on my mind: chili takes a lot of cash up front and the hired labor bill is heavy, but the margin is good when price holds. If I wanted safer I'd put more into wheat-maize, but on 225 mu I need some higher-value crops to pay the wages.
